original_question: Let A be an R-sectorial operator on an L^p-space with p in (1, infinity). Must the sectorial angle omega(A) equal the R-sectorial angle omega_R(A)? The same question is asked under stronger semigroup assumptions: if -A generates an analytic C_0-semigroup, does the equality still hold when the semigroup is positive, contractive, or both positive and contractive?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 (Introduction), read together with the immediately following Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right mathematical target: the paper’s angle-equality conjecture for R-sectorial operators on L^p-spaces, together with its three stronger semigroup variants asking the same question under positivity, contractivity, and positivity plus contractivity of the analytic C_0-semigroup generated by -A.
missing_details: The paper works with complex Banach spaces; this should be stated explicitly.
The ambient space should be specified as an L_p-space L_p(Ω) with 1 < p < ∞, rather than just 'an L^p-space' informally.
Under the paper’s convention, a sectorial operator is closed, densely defined, and has dense range; this is part of the standing setup behind ω(A).
R-sectoriality should be understood in the paper’s standard sense, with ω_R(A) defined as the infimum of the angles for which the resolvent family is R-bounded.
In the semigroup cases, -A should be said to generate a bounded analytic C_0-semigroup on the same L_p-space.
The meanings of 'positive' and 'contractive' should be made explicit: positivity and contractivity are properties of the real semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0}.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should separate the four cases clearly: the general R-sectorial case, the positive analytic case, the contractive analytic case, and the positive contractive analytic case.
The paper’s intent is specifically about equality of the sectorial and R-sectorial angles, not merely about maximal regularity or about whether ω_R(A) < π/2.
refined_question: Let 1 < p < ∞, let L_p(Ω) be a complex L_p-space, and let A be an R-sectorial operator on L_p(Ω), where sectorial operators are understood in the paper’s convention as closed, densely defined operators with dense range. Must the sectorial angle and the R-sectorial angle coincide, i.e. is ω(A) = ω_R(A)? More specifically, if -A generates a bounded analytic C_0-semigroup (T(z)) on L_p(Ω), does this angle equality still hold in each of the following three stronger situations: (i) T(t) is positive for every t ≥ 0; (ii) T(t) is contractive on L_p(Ω) for every t ≥ 0; (iii) T(t) is both positive and contractive for every t ≥ 0?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target: it singles out exactly the angle-equality problem posed in the introduction and includes the three semigroup-strengthened variants that the paper isolates nearby. What it lacked was the paper’s standing operator-theoretic setup (complex Banach spaces, sectorial operators with dense range, and the precise semigroup-side interpretation of positivity and contractivity), so the refinement mainly makes those implicit conventions explicit without broadening the scope. I did not replace the conjectural question by the nearby theorem, because Theorem 1.3 is presented as a partial positive result around Conjecture 1.1 rather than as the main target itself.
